components.gap: Conservativity is stated and proved only for a definitional extension by a single relation symbol (handbook/restoration/inherited-03729-03907.tex 108-169; handbook/parts/p02/first-order-languages-structures-and-substitution-w02b-p02-018.tex 206-241 with proofs at handbook/annex/p02/first-order-languages-structures-and-substitution-w02b-p02-018.tex 254-361). Definitional extensions by function and constant symbols, with the required existence/uniqueness (unique-value) premise on the defining formula relative to T, are not defined, and no expansion or conservativity result is proved for them; the packet chapter itself says so (handbook/parts/p02/first-order-languages-structures-and-substitution-w02b-p02-018.tex 362-368). The handbook nevertheless includes such extensions elsewhere on the route: handbook/parts/p14/strength-consistency-and-independence.tex 322-327 (definitional expansion and its base: the actual defining axioms and unique-value conditions are required) and handbook/parts/p05/models-and-interpretability-supplement.tex 258-264 (a definitional extension interprets back into its base by replacing each new symbol by its defining formula). Missing: the function/constant case with its uniqueness premises and its conservativity proof.
